title: Tree-unrolling preserves the value of a node
statement: Let $F$ be a Boolean feedforward circuit whose inputs are indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$, and suppose each of its gates has finite arity and computes either the conjunction or the disjunction of its inputs, according to a flag marking every non-input node as an AND node or an OR node. Then for every layer $m$ with $m \le \mathrm{depth}(F)$, every node $v$ of layer $m$, and every input assignment $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2$, the Boolean circuit obtained by tree-unrolling $v$, evaluated at $x$, equals the value that $v$ takes in $F$ under the assignment $x$.
hypotheses_covered: F is a Boolean feedforward circuit with inputs indexed by Fin n
every gate is the conjunction or disjunction of its inputs per the AND/OR flag (hcorrect, isAnd)
m is a layer index with m ≤ depth(F)
v is a node at layer m
x is an input assignment Fin n → Bool
replaced:
If every gate of $F$ is an AND or OR gate as recorded by $\texttt{isAnd}$ and
$\texttt{gfin}$, then for every node $v$ at layer $m$ and every input
$x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \{0,1\}$,
\[
(\texttt{nodeToCircuit}\ F\ \texttt{isAnd}\ \texttt{gfin}\ m\ h\ v).\texttt{eval}\ x
 = F.\texttt{evalNode}\ v\ x .
\]
